questions.question: What is the purpose of the 3D UI (User Interface) overlays in game design?
options: To draw 2D labels, scores, and health bars directly on top of the 3D game screen!
questions.explanation: Correct! UI overlays display dashboard info (like points, health, or alerts) over the camera view.

questions.question: Which block is used to add text overlays onto your active 3D HUD canvas?
questions.explanation: Excellent! 'add UI text' draws scoreboards and HUD data overlays onto specific flat screen coordinates.

questions.question: Why do sounds matter so much in interactive video games?
options: They make the computer run faster
They bring life, atmosphere, and instant audio feedback (like blast alarms or success bells) to gameplay!
questions.explanation: Perfect! Sound design enhances atmosphere and guides player feedback during events.

questions.question: What block is used to play a victory fanfare or laser blast sound from the Audio libraries?
questions.explanation: Spot on! 'play sound wave' launches loaded sound effects immediately when triggered.

questions.question: How can you display a glowing start button to players before the 3D game loads?
options: By adding a UI button overlay that hides itself and starts gameplay loops when clicked
questions.explanation: Great! Pre-game screens use overlay UI buttons that initialize variables and clear templates on click.

questions.question: In our Duck Hunter HUD, which block increases a global variable 'Score' by 10 points when a duck clone is eliminated?
questions.explanation: Perfect! The 'change variable by' block increments scores (e.g. +10 per successful hit).

questions.question: Which block clears the UI text overlays when transitioning from the start screen to active gameplay?
options: clear UI overlays / hide UI panel
questions.explanation: Spot on! Hiding start overlays cleans the screen, revealing the 3D gaming space.

questions.question: What component triggers victory conditions when the player's score reaching 100 points?
options: An if statement checking if Score = 100
questions.explanation: Great! Logic checks (if score = 100 then show win screen) automate win conditions.

questions.question: What type of sound library should you search to find a laser sound effect for our rifle?
options: Sci-Fi / Space drawer in Sound Library
questions.explanation: Perfect! Laser blasts are Sci-Fi category files, fitting sci-fi crosshairs.

questions.question: How can you prevent shooting inputs from firing while the start screen overlay is active?
options: Use a global game variable 'game_active' (only fire if game_active = True)
questions.explanation: Perfect! Checking state variables (e.g. game_active = true) ensures scripts only run during active phases.

questions.question: Coding Task: Write block pseudo-code to display a UI text overlay saying 'Score: ' joined with the global variable 'Score' at coordinates X=20, Y=20.
questions.task_hint: add UI text(label=join('Score: ', get global Score), x=20, y=20)
questions.explanation: Outstanding! This displays a dynamic, self-updating score monitor on the player's HUD canvas!

questions.question: Coding Task: Write block pseudo-code to play a sound wave named 'victory_fanfare' and stop all scripts when a win check passes.
questions.explanation: Perfect! Audio cues combined with stop loops create neat, satisfying game conclusions!
